Random beacon sampling demands work proofs from a subset of identities and tends to defeat sybil farming, since attackers cannot predict which clones are examined.

Every epoch, a random function selects 5% of identities, which must file a beacon proof in 2 epochs, 7 jurors; a miss freezes rewards 6 epochs, a second miss slashes 50%, and a gale of checks sweeps the population.

For 1,000 clones locked at 120 units, 5% sampled each epoch means 50 clones are examined each round; 30% missed proofs cost 6,000 units a round, while the comet of penalties makes hoarding futile.
